# Alibaba Cloud Apsara Stack v3.18.6-2607 DataWorks Developer Guide 20260831

## API introduction

This topic lists the DataWorks OpenAPI operations.

**OpenAPI**

DataWorks OpenAPI covers tenant, metadata, DataStudio, Data Integration, Operation Center, Data Quality, DataService Studio, scheduling, Data Protection, Migration Assistant, Data Modeling, Security Center, and Open Platform:

## Prerequisites

### Obtain an AccessKey pair

AccessKey pairs are classified into AccessKey pairs assigned by Resource Access Management (RAM) and those assigned by Security Token Service (STS). You can use either type of AccessKey pair for authentication when you call operations. This topic describes how to obtain an AccessKey pair that is assigned by RAM.

**Background information**

An AccessKey pair is used to verify the identity of a request sender. An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret that are used to implement symmetric encryption. The AccessKey ID is used to identify a user. The AccessKey secret is used to encrypt a signature string. You can use RAM or STS to assign an AccessKey pair for authentication. Use RAM to assign an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret to a third party. Use STS to assign an AccessKey ID, an AccessKey secret, and a security token to a third party. For more information, see Obtain an AccessKey pair assigned by STS. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides AccessKey pairs for personal accounts and organizations. Only operations administrators and the administrators of level-1 organizations can obtain the AccessKey pairs of organizations. We recommend that you use the AccessKey pairs of personal accounts to call the operations provided by the Apsara Unimanager Management Console and cloud services. If you use the AccessKey pair of a personal account, configure the request headers that are described in the following table for access control. Otherwise, an error that indicates insufficient permissions may occur.

**Warning**

The AccessKey pair of a personal account is managed by the permission system of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. If you need to obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, make sure that your operation is allowed by an administrator. This ensures security.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| x-acs-regionid | The ID of the region. Example: cn-hangzhou-*. |
| x-acs-organizationid | The ID of the organization in the Apsara Uni- manager Management Console. For more information about how to obtain organization IDs, see the GetOrganizationList section in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Developer Guide. |
| x-acs-resourcegroupid | The ID of the resource set in the Apsara Uni- manager Management Console. For more information about how to obtain resource set IDs, see the ListResourceGroup section in Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Developer Guide. |
| x-acs-instanceid | The ID of the instance that you want to manage. If you want to obtain the ID of an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance, you can obtain the ID from the ECS instance list. |

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account**

To obtain the AccessKey pair of a personal account, perform the following steps:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the upper-right corner of the homepage, click the profile picture and then click **User**
**Information**.
3. In the **AccessKey Pair** section, view the AccessKey pair of your account.

**Note**

An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. These credentials provide full permissions on cloud resources within your account. You must keep the AccessKey pair confidential.

**Obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization**

To obtain the AccessKey pair of an organization, perform the following steps:
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Resources > Organizations**.
4. In the organization list, click the name of the level-1 organization whose AccessKey pair you
want to obtain.
5. Click **Management Accesskey**.
6. In the dialog box that appears, view the AccessKey pair of the organization.

## Use the POP gateway to

**call Apsara Stack API**

**operations**

This topic provides a complete Java SDK integration guide for calling Apsara Stack DataWorks API operations through the POP gateway. It includes the configuration of key parameters, such as the service endpoint, AccessKey pair, service name, region ID, and endpoint name, authentication logic, and call examples.

**Important**

The DataWorks HTTP API is deprecated. Migrate to the Java SDK as soon as possible.

**Service endpoint**

The endpoint that is used to access DataWorks. The endpoint consists of the prefix dataworks-public or dataworks-public-vpc and the domain name of DataWorks. For example, the URL that is used to access Apsara Stack DataWorks is http://ide.envxxx.yyyyy.com. Common endpoint: The endpoint is prefixed with `dataworks-public` . The endpoint is

```
 dataworks-public.envxxx.yyyyy.com .
```

Virtual private cloud (VPC) endpoint: The endpoint is prefixed with `dataworks-public-vpc` . The endpoint is `dataworks-public-vpc.envxxx.yyyyy.com` .

**Note**

The DataWorks POP gateway now supports IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack. To use the IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack capabilities of the service, contact Alibaba Cloud Technical Support to complete the platform-side IPv6 prerequisite transformation and enable the IPv6 feature for the service. For more information, see the **Network Changes > Feature**
**Orchestration > IPv6 Dashboard** section in **Apsara Stack VPC O&M Guide**.

*************************************

Use the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret of your Apsara Stack tenant account.

**Service name**

Set the service name to `dataworks-public` .

**Region ID and endpoint name**

RegionId: the ID of the region, which is fixed as default. EndpointName: the name of the endpoint, which is fixed as default.

**Authorization**

For Alibaba Cloud Apsara Stack Enterprise V3.13 and later, you can call API operations by using DataWorks SDK for Java without authorization.

**Call an API operation by using DataWorks SDK for Java**

eway to call Apsara Stack API op erations After you send an API request that contains specified parameters from a client to the endpoint, the request is forwarded to pctowap open platform (POP) API Gateway for authentication. If the request fails the authentication, an error is returned. If the authentication is successful, the request is forwarded to the corresponding API operation. If the request is successful, a response is returned.

**Sample code**

```java
import com.aliyuncs.DefaultAcsClient; import com.aliyuncs.IAcsClient; import com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ClientException; import com.aliyuncs.exceptions.ServerException; import com.aliyuncs.profile.DefaultProfile; import com.google.gson.Gson; import java.util.*; import com.aliyuncs.dataworks_public.model.v20200518.*; public class GetDataServiceApi {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        DefaultProfile profile = DefaultProfile.getProfile("cn-qingdao", "
<accessKeyId>", "<accessSecret>");
        DefaultProfile.addEndpoint("", "dataworks-public", "endpoint");
        IAcsClient client = new DefaultAcsClient(profile);
        GetDataServiceApiRequest request = new GetDataServiceApiRequest();
        request.setTenantId(123);
        request.setProjectId(123);
        request.setApiId(123);
        try {
            GetDataServiceApiResponse response = client.getAcsResponse(request);
            System.out.println(new Gson().toJson(response));
        } catch (ServerException e) {
            e.printStackTrace();
        } catch (ClientException e) {
            System.out.println("ErrCode:" + e.getErrCode());
            System.out.println("ErrMsg:" + e.getErrMsg());
            System.out.println("RequestId:" + e.getRequestId());
```

## OpenAPI

### Tenants

#### CreateProject

Calls the CreateProject operation to create a project.

**Request headers**

The CreateProject operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the Common request parameters topic.

**Request parameters**

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RegionId | Strin g | Host | Yes | default | The region ID. |
| ProjectNa me | Strin g | Query | Yes | autotest | The name of the compute engine or data source. |
| ProjectDe scription | Strin g | Query | Yes | test describe _ | The description of the workspace. |
| DisableDe velopmen t | Boole an | Query | No | false | Specifies whether to disable the Development role. Valid values: false : The Development role is enabled. This is the default value. true : The Development role is disabled. |
| IsAllowDo wnload | Integ er | Query | No | 1 | Specifies whether query result download from DataStudio is allowed. Valid values: 1 : Download is allowed. This is the default value. 0 : Download is not allowed. |

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

#### ListCalcEngines

Queries a list of compute engine instances.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | ListCalcEngines | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to ListCalcEngines. |
| CalcEngineType | String | Yes | ODPS | The type of the compute engine instance. Valid values: ODPS, EMR, BLINK, HOLO, MaxGraph, HYBRIDDB FOR POSTGRESQL, _ _ ADB MYSQL, and HADOOP CDH. The _ _ values are not case-sensitive. |
| Name | String | Yes | abc | The name of the compute engine instance, which must be exactly matched. |
| ProjectId | Long | Yes | 27 | The ID of the DataWorks workspace with which the compute engine instance is associated. |
| RegionId | String | Yes | default | The region ID. The value of this parameter is fixed as default. |
| EnvType | String | No | PRD | The environment in which the compute engine instance runs. Valid values: DEV and PRD. The value DEV indicates the development environment, and the value PRD indicates the production environment. |
| PageSize | Integer | No | 10 | The number of entries per page. Valid values: 1 to 20. Default value: 10. |
| PageNumber | Integer | No | 1 | The page number. Pages start from page 1. Default value: 1. |

#### UpdateFile

Updates an existing file node. You must change at least one parameter from its original value. For example, if a parameter is originally set to `A` , you must change it to a new value, such as `B` . Submitting a request with all original values returns an `invalid` error.

**Request headers**

This operation uses only common request headers. See common request parameters for details.

**Request parameters**

| Content | Strin g | Body | No | SELECT "1"; | The code content of the file. The code format varies based on the file type ( fileType ). To view the specific code format, go to the Operations Center in the DataWorks console, right-click a task of the corresponding type, and then select View Code. |
| RegionId | Strin g | Host | Yes | default | The region ID. The value of this parameter is fixed at default. |
| AutoRerun Times | Integ er | Body | No | 3 | The number of automatic reruns after a failure. |
| AutoRerun IntervalMil lis | Integ er | Body | No | 120000 | The interval between automatic reruns, in milliseconds. The maximum value is 1,800,000 milliseconds, which is 30 minutes. This parameter corresponds to the Rerun Interval setting on the Time Properties tab in the scheduling configuration section of a Data Development task in the DataWorks console. In the console, the rerun interval is specified in minutes. You must convert the unit from minutes to milliseconds when calling this operation. |

| Parame ter | Typ e | Locati on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RerunMod e | Strin g | Body | No | ALL ALLOWED _ | The rerun policy. This parameter corresponds to the Rerun Property setting on the Time Properties tab in the scheduling configuration section of a Data Development task in the DataWorks console. Valid values: FAILURE ALLOWED : _ The node can be rerun only if it fails to run. ALL DENIED : The _ node cannot be rerun regardless of whether it succeeds or fails to run. ALL ALLOWED : The _ node can be rerun regardless of whether it succeeds or fails to run. |
| Stop | Boole an | Body | No | false | Specifies whether to pause the scheduling of the node. This parameter corresponds to the Pause Scheduling option for the Scheduling Type setting. You can find this setting on the Time Properties tab in the scheduling configuration section of a Data Development task in the DataWorks console. Valid values: true : pauses the scheduling of the node. false : does not pause the scheduling of the node. |

### Data Integration

#### CreateDISyncTask

Creates a data synchronization node of Data Integration. DataWorks only allows you to call the CreateDISyncTask operation to create Data Integration offline synchronization tasks. To Data Integration a real-time synchronization task or a solution synchronization task, you must call the GenerateDISyncTaskConfigForCreating and QueryDISyncTaskConfigProcessResult operations to obtain the parameters that are required to asynchronously generate a Data Integration synchronization task. Then, you can use the parameters as input parameters of the CreateDISyncTask operation to create a real-time synchronization task or a solution synchronization task by using the CreateDISyncTask operation.

### Data modeling

#### QueryPublicModelEngine

Queries the information about objects created in Data Modeling.

**Usage notes**

Each time you call this API operation, you must specify a fast modeling language (FML) statement that you want to use to query information about objects created in Data Modeling. The information about the objects created in Data Modeling can be queried by page, except for data layers, business processes, and data domains. You can add the `offset num limit` `num` statement to an FML statement. The offset num limit num statement specifies the offset when the information about the objects is queried and the number of pages to return each time. The offset value must be a multiple of the number of pages to return. Up to 1,000 entries can be returned each time you call this API operation.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Posit ion | Required | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Text | Strin g | Body | Yes | show dim tables | The FML statement that is used to query information about the objects created in Data Modeling. Only SHOW statements are supported. |
| ProjectId | Strin g | Body | Yes | 1234 | The ID of the DataWorks workspace. You can log on to the DataWorks console and go to the Workspace Management page to obtain the workspace ID. |
| RegionId | Strin g | Host | No | default | The region in which DataWorks is activated. Set the value to default. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| ReturnValue | Map | [ { "gmtModified": The time when the table was last modified, "code": "The table name", "creatorId": "The ID of the user who created the table", "creatorName": "The name of the user who created the table", "modifierId": "The ID of the user who last modified the table", "gmtCreate": The time when the table was created, "type": The type of the table, "ownerId": "The ID of the table owner", "uuid": "The table ID", "businessUnitUuid" : "The business unit ID", "detailType": "The subtype of the table", "ownerName": "The name of the table owner", "name": "The display name of the table", "modifierName": "The name of the user who last modified the table", "businessProcessU uid": "The business process ID" } ] | The information about the object created in Data Modeling. |
| RequestId | String | 4CFB2DED-7D9B- 4C42-B4AA- CFF4991D**** | The request ID. You can query logs and troubleshoot issues based on the request ID. |

#### CreateRemind

**Request headers**

| NodeIds | Strin g | Body | No | 1,2,3 | The node IDs. This parameter is valid only when RemindUnit is set to NODE . Separate multiple node IDs with commas (,). A single rule can monitor a maximum of 50 nodes. |

|   | NODE |
|---|---|
| BASELINE |   |
| PROJECT |   |

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |

| BizProcess Ids | Strin g | Body | No | 1,2,3 | The business process IDs. This parameter is valid only when RemindUnit is set to BIZPROCESS . Separate multiple business process IDs with commas (,). A single rule can monitor a maximum of 5 business processes. |

#### GetDag

Queries the information about a directed acyclic graph (DAG) based on the ID of the DAG. You can call the GetDag operation to query the information about the DAG for a manually triggered workflow, a manually triggered node, or a data backfill instance. However, you cannot query the information about the DAG for an auto triggered node or an auto triggered workflow.

Queries the information about a custom alert rule.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Requir ed | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Action | String | Yes | GetRemind | The operation that you want to perform. Set the value to GetRemind. |

| RemindId | Long | Yes | 1234 | The custom alert rule ID. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Data | Struct |   | The details of the custom alert rule. |
| AlertInterval | Integer | 1800 | The minimum interval at which alerts are reported. Unit: seconds. |
| AlertMethods | List | SMS,MAIL | The notification method. Valid values: MAIL, SMS, and PHONE. The value MAIL indicates that the notification is sent by email. The value SMS indicates that the notification is sent by text message. The value PHONE indicates that the notification is sent by phone call. Only DataWorks Professional Edition and more advanced editions support the PHONE notification method. You can specify multiple notification methods. Separate them with commas (,). |
| AlertTargets | List | 952795279527952 7 | If the value of the AlertUnit parameter is OWNER, this parameter is left empty. If the value of the AlertUnit parameter is OTHER, the ID of the Apsara Stack tenant account used by the specified user is returned. Multiple IDs are separated by commas (,). |

| AlertUnit | String | OWNER | The recipient of the alert. Valid values: OWNER and OTHER. The value OWNER indicates the node owner. The value OTHER indicates a specified user. |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baselines | Array of Baselines |   | The baselines to which the custom alert rule is applied. This parameter is returned if the value of the RemindUnit parameter is BASELINE. |
| BaselineId | Long | 1234 | The ID of the baseline. |
| BaselineName | String | Baseline name | The name of the baseline. |
| BizProcesses | Array of BizProcesses |   | The workflows to which the custom alert rule is applied. This parameter is returned if the value of the RemindUnit parameter is BIZPROCESS. |
| BizId | Long | 9527 | The workflow ID. |
| BizProcessNa me | String | Workflow name | The name of the workflow. |

| Detail | String | {"hour":23,"minu": 59} | If the value of the RemindType parameter is FINISHED, this parameter is left empty. If the value of the RemindType parameter is UNFINISHED, the trigger conditions are returned as key-value pairs. Example: {"hour":23,"minu":59}. Valid values of hour: 0 to 47. Valid values of minu: 0 to 59. If the value of the RemindType parameter is ERROR, this parameter is left empty. If the value of the RemindType parameter is CYCLE UNFINISHED, the _ trigger conditions are returned as key- value pairs. Example: {"1":"05:50","2":"06:50","3":"07:50","4": "08:50","5":"09:50","6":"10:50","7":"11: 50","8":"12:50","9":"13:50","10":"14:50" ,"11":"15:50","12":"16:50","13":"17:50", "14":"18:50","15":"19:50","16":"20:50"," 17":"21:50","18":"22:50","19":"23:50"," 20":"24:50","21":"25:50"}. The key indicates the ID of the cycle. Valid values: 1 to 288. The value indicates the timeout period of the node that is running in the cycle. The value is in the hh:mm format. Valid values of hh: 0 to 47. Valid values of mm: 0 to 59. If the value of the RemindType parameter is TIMEOUT, the timeout period is returned. Unit: seconds. Example: 1800. This value indicates that an alert is reported if the node is run for more than 30 minutes. |
|---|---|---|---|
| DndEnd | String | 08:00 | The end time of the quiet hours. The value is in the hh:mm format. Valid values of hh: 0 to 23. Valid values of mm: 0 to 59. |
| DndStart | String | 00:00 | The start time of the quiet hours. The value is in the hh:mm format. Valid values of hh: 0 to 23. Valid values of mm: 0 to 59. |
| Founder | String | 9527951795**** | The ID of the Apsara Stack tenant account used by the creator of the custom alert rule. |
| MaxAlertTimes | Integer | 3 | The maximum number of alerts. |

#### ListDags

Queries a list of directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) for a single data backfill instance based on OpSeq. Supported DAG types: MANUAL: the DAG for a manually triggered workflow. SMOKE_TEST: the DAG for a smoke testing workflow. SUPPLY_DATA: the DAG for a data backfill instance. BUSINESS_PROCESS_DAG: the DAG for a one-time workflow. Supported DAG states: CREATED: The DAG is created. RUNNING: The DAG is running. FAILURE: The DAG fails to run. SUCCESS: The DAG is successfully run.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request parameters**

WAIT RESOURCE: The node is waiting _ for resources. RUNNING: The instance is running. CHECKING: Data quality is being checked for the node. CHECKING CONDITION: Branch _ conditions are being checked for the node. FAILURE: The node fails to be run. SUCCESS: The node is successfully run. |
| -CycTime | Long | 1590422400000 | The time when the node started to be run. This value is a UNIX timestamp representing the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC. |
| - BeginRunning Time | Long | 1590416703313 | The time when the instance started to be run. This value is a UNIX timestamp representing the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC. |
| -FinishTime | Long | 1590416703313 | The time when the node ended. This value is a UNIX timestamp representing the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since January 1, 1970, 00:00:00 UTC. |

MANUAL(1): The node is a manually triggered node. The node is not regularly run. PAUSE(2): The node is a frozen node. The scheduling system still regularly runs the node but sets the node status to Failed when the scheduling system starts to run the node. SKIP(3): The node is a dry-run node. The scheduling system regularly runs the node but sets the status of the node to succeeded when the scheduling system starts to run the node. SKIP UNCHOOSE(4): The node is an _ unselected node in a temporary workflow. This type of node exists only in temporary workflows. The scheduling system sets the status of the node to successful when the scheduling system starts to run the node. SKIP CYCLE(5): The node is a node that _ is scheduled by the week or month and is waiting for the scheduling time to arrive. The scheduling system regularly runs the node but sets the node status to successful when the scheduling system starts to run the node. CONDITION UNCHOOSE(6): The node is _ not selected by its ancestor branch node and is run as a dry-run node. REALTIME DEPRECATED(7): The node _ has instances that are generated in real time but deprecated. The scheduling system sets the status of the node to successful. |

MANUAL(1): The node is a manually triggered node. The node is not regularly run. PAUSE(2): The node is a frozen node. The scheduling system regularly runs the node but sets the status of the node to failed when the scheduling system starts to run the node. SKIP(3): The node is a dry-run node. The scheduling system still regularly runs the node but sets the node status to Succeeded when the scheduling system starts to run the node. SKIP UNCHOOSE(4): The node is an _ unselected node in a temporary workflow. This type of node exists only in temporary workflows. The scheduling system sets the node status to Succeeded when the scheduling system starts to run the node. SKIP CYCLE(5): The node is a node that _ is scheduled by week or month and is waiting for the scheduling time to arrive. The scheduling system regularly runs the node but sets the node status to Succeeded when the scheduling system starts to run the node. CONDITION UNCHOOSE(6): The node is _ not selected by its ancestor branch node and is run as a dry-run node. REALTIME DEPRECATED(7): The node _ has instances that are generated in real time but deprecated. The scheduling system sets the node status to Succeeded. |

Valid values: FINISHED, UNFINISHED, ERROR, CYCLE UNFINISHED, and TIMEOUT. _ The value FINISHED indicates that the node finishes running. The value UNFINISHED indicates that the node is still running at the specified point in time. The value ERROR indicates that an error occurs when the node is running. The value CYCLE UNFINISHED indicates that _ the node does not finish running in the specified scheduling cycle. The value TIMEOUT indicates that the node times out. You can specify multiple conditions. Separate them with commas (,). |

Only DataWorks Professional Edition and more advanced editions support the PHONE notification method. |

Configure NodeParameters in the following JSON format: {"<ID of a node in the manually triggered workflow>": "Scheduling parameter settings of the node, which are in the same format as the parameter settings in the Parameters section of the Properties tab on the DataStudio page", "<ID of a node in the manually triggered workflow>": "Scheduling parameter settings of the node, which are in the same format as the parameter settings in the Parameters section of the Properties tab on the DataStudio page"}. |

#### UpdateRemind

**Request parameters**

The value NODE indicates that the monitored object is a node. The value BASELINE indicates that the monitored object is a baseline. The value PROJECT indicates that the monitored object is a workspace. The value BIZPROCESS indicates that the monitored object is a workflow. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NodeIds | String | No | 1,2,3 | The ID of the node to which the custom alert rule is applied. This parameter takes effect if the RemindUnit parameter is set to NODE. You can specify multiple IDs. Separate multiple IDs with commas (,). A maximum of 50 nodes can be specified for a custom alert rule. |

You can specify multiple IDs. Separate multiple IDs with commas (,). A maximum of five baselines can be specified for a custom alert rule. |
| ProjectId | Long | No | 1234 | The ID of the workspace to which the custom alert rule is applied. This parameter takes effect when the RemindUnit parameter is set to PROJECT. You can specify only one workspace for a custom alert rule. |
| BizProcessIds | String | No | 1,2,3 | The ID of the workflow to which the custom alert rule is applied. This parameter takes effect when the RemindUnit parameter is set to BIZPROCESS. You can specify multiple IDs. Separate multiple IDs with commas (,). A maximum of five workflows can be specified for a custom alert rule. |

| RemindType | String | No | FINISHED | The conditions that trigger an alert. Valid values: FINISHED, UNFINISHED, ERROR, CYCLE UNFINISHED, and _ TIMEOUT. The value FINISHED indicates that the node is run. The value UNFINISHED indicates that the node is still running at the specified point in time. The value ERROR indicates that an error occurs when the node is running. The value CYCLE UNFINISHED indicates that _ the node is still running in the specified cycle. The value TIMEOUT indicates that the node times out. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MaxAlertTimes | Integer | No | 3 | The maximum number of alerts. Valid values: 1 to 10. Default value: 3. |
| AlertInterval | Integer | No | 1800 | The minimum interval at which alerts are reported. Unit: seconds. Minimum value: 1200. Default value: 1800. |

| Detail | String | No | {"hour":23,"min u":59} | The details of the conditions that trigger an alert. If the RemindType parameter is set to FINISHED, leave this parameter empty. If the RemindType parameter is set to UNFINISHED, configure this parameter as key-value pairs. Example: {"hour":23,"minu":59}. Valid values of hour: 0 to 47. Valid values of minu: 0 to 59. If the RemindType parameter is set to ERROR, leave this parameter empty. If the RemindType parameter is set to CYCLE UNFINISHED, _ configure this parameter as key- value pairs. Example: {"1":"05:50","2":"06:50","3":"07:5 0","4":"08:50","5":"09:50","6":"10: 50","7":"11:50","8":"12:50","9":"13 :50","10":"14:50","11":"15:50","12 ":"16:50","13":"17:50","14":"18:50 ","15":"19:50","16":"20:50","17":"2 1:50","18":"22:50","19":"23:50","2 0":"24:50","21":"25:50"}. The key indicates the ID of the cycle. Valid values: 1 to 288. The value indicates the timeout period of the node that is running in the cycle. The value is in the hh:mm format. Valid values of hh: 0 to 47. Valid values of mm: 0 to 59. If the RemindType parameter is set to TIMEOUT, set this parameter to the timeout period. Unit: seconds. Example: 1800. This value indicates that an alert is reported if the node has run for more than 30 minutes. |

#### UpdateQualityRule

**Important**

If a quality rule is based on a fixed value, you must specify the `Operator` and `ExpectValue` parameters. If the quality rule is a dynamic threshold rule, which includes custom rules and templatebased rules, you must set the `Trend` parameter to `up` , `down` , or `abs` . The `CriticalThreshold` and `WarningThreshold` parameters cannot both be empty.

The following sample code describes the three parts of RuleDetailJson: `{`

```json
 "contentRule": {
     "dataType": "Landline number",
     "regExp": null
```

`},`

```json
 "metaRules": [{
     "compareType": "equal",
     "param": "a.b.c",
     "metaType": "guid",
 }],
 "excludeMetaRules": [{
     "compareType": "equal",
     "param": "c.d.e",
     "metaType": "guid",
```

`}]` `}` Parameters:
**ContentRule**: the content identification rule. You must configure ContentRule or
MetaRules. The content identification rule contains the **rule name** and **rule content**. The rule name can be the name of a built-in rule, a regular expression, a self-generated data identification model, or a sample library. If the rule name matches a specific regular expression, the rule content expresses the regular content.
**metaRules**: the rule for scanning fields. You must configure metaRules or ContentRule.
This rule contains the **rule name** and **rule content**. The rule name is fixed, which can be identified by metadata. The rule content is speficied by using **compareType**, **param**, and
**metaType**.
**compareType**: the comparison type. Valid values: **equal** and **regexp**. If the value of the
param parameter contains an asterisk (*), set compareType to **regexp**. Otherwise, set compareType to **equal**.
**param**: the fields that you want to scan. Wildcards are supported. onfigure param in the
`project.table.column` format. For example, if you set param to a.b.c, fields in the Column c of Table b in the Project a are to be scanned. If you set param to a.b., fields in any column of Table b in Project a are to be scanned.
**metaType**: the type of metadata. Set the value to guid.
**excludeMetaRules**: the rule for excluding the fields to be scanned. This parameter is
optional. The rule contains the **rule name** and **rule content**. The **rule name** and **rule**
**content** are the same as these specified by **metaRules**.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Name | Strin g | Query | Yes | [ {"dbType":"hologres","in stanceName":"ABC","dat abaseName":"abc"}, {"dbType":"ODPS.ODPS" ,"projectName":"adbc"} ] | The parameters that you can configure to query the access records. Valid values: dbType instanceName databaseName projectName clusterName The following example shows the parameters configured to query the access records of the sensitive data in the abc database of the Hologres instance ABC: [ {"dbType":"hologres","i nstanceName":"ABC","d atabaseName":"abc"} ]. You must configure the parameters based on the compute engine that you use in your business. |
| PageSize | Integ er | Query | Yes | 1 | The number of entries per page. Valid values: 1 to 1000. |
| PageNo | Integ er | Query | Yes | 100 | The page number. Valid values: 1 to 1000. |

|   | Developer Gui | de·Open | API |   |   | DataWork | s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| OpType | Strin g | Query | No | SQL SELECT _ | The operation that is performed on the data. Valid values: SQL SELECT: specifies _ the data access operation. For example, you can execute the SELECT statement to query the data. TUNNEL DOWNLOAD: _ specifies the data download operation. For example, you can run a Tunnel command to download data. |

**Request headers**

|   | Strin |   |   |   |   |

Details of the RuleDetailJson parameter:

**ContentRule**

: Specifies the content identification rule. You must specify either this parameter or `MetaRules` . A `ContentRule` includes a **rule name** and **rule content** . The rule name can be a built-in rule name or `Regex match` . If the rule name is `Regex` `match` , the rule content must be the corresponding regular expression.

**metaRules**

: The field scan rule. You can specify either this parameter or `ContentRule` . `metaRules` contains a **rule name** and **rule content** . The rule name is a fixed value that is identified by metadata identification. The rule content contains **compareType** ,

**param**

, and **metaType** .

**compareType**

: The comparison type. Valid values are **equal** and **regexp** . If the `param` value contains a wildcard (*), set this parameter to **regexp** . Otherwise, set it to **equal** .

**param**

: The path for the field scan, which can include the wildcard character (*). The format is `project.table.column` . For example, `a.b.c` matches the column named `c` in the table named `b` within the project named `a` . `a.b.*` matches any column in the table named `b` within the project named `a` .

**metaType**

: The metadata matching type. This parameter must be set to the fixed value `guid` .

**excludeMetaRules**

: The rules to exclude from field scans. This parameter is optional. It contains a **rule name** and **rule content** that must match the **rule name** and **rule**

**content**

of a rule in **metaRules** .

|---|---|---|

**_clazz**

: The `name` field corresponds to `dataType` , and `templateJsonStr` corresponds to `_clazz` .

If LabelSecurity is disabled for the MaxCompute project in which you want to request permissions on the fields of a table, or the security level of the fields is 0 or is lower than or equal to the security level of the Alibaba Cloud account for which you want to request permissions, you can request only permanent permissions. You can go to the Workspace Management page of the DataWorks console, click MaxCompute Management in the left-side navigation pane, and then check whether column-level access control is enabled. #### GetExtension

Queries the information about an extension.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request parameters**

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RegionId | Strin g | Host | No | default | The region ID. Set the value to default. |
| Extension Code | Strin g | Query | Yes | ce4*********086da5 | The unique code of the extension. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | 0000-ABCD-EFG | The request ID. You can query logs and troubleshoot issues based on the request ID. |
| Extension | Struct |   | The extension details. |
| -BindEventList | Array |   | The extension points. |
| --EventCode | String | commit-file | The code of the extension point event. |
| --EventName | String | Pre-event for file committing | The name of the extension point event. |
| - EventCategory List | Array |   | The event types. |
| -- CategoryCode | String | file-change | The code of the event type. |
| -- CategoryName | String | File change event | The name of the event type. |
| - ExtensionCode | String | ce4*********086da 5 | The unique code of the extension. |
| - ExtensionNam e | String | Extension name | The extension name. |
| - ExtensionDesc | String | This is a description. | The extension description. |
| -HelpDocUrl | String | https://www.aliyun. com/ | The URL of the help documentation of the extension. |
| -Status | Integer | 0 | The extension state. Valid values: 0: Testing. 1: Publishing. 3: Disabled. 4: Approving. 5: Approved. 6: Approve Failed. |
| -ProjectTesting | Long | 13552 | The workspace for testing. If the extension is being tested, the extension can be used only in the workspace for testing. |

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| -DetailUrl | String | https://www.aliyun. com/ | The URL of the extension details page, on which you can view the details of the process blocked by the extension. |
| - ParameterSett ing | String | extension.project.d isabled=projectId1, projectId2,projectId 3 | The parameter settings. |
| -OptionSetting | String | Options | The options defined for the extension. |

**Examples**

Sample requests

```
http(s)://[Endpoint]/?Action=GetExtension &ExtensionCode=ce4*********086da5 &Common request parameters
```

Sample success responses `JSON` format `{`

```json
 "Extension":{
  "Status":0,
  "ExtensionName":"Extension name",
  "ParameterSetting":"extension.project.disabled=projectId1,projectId2,projectId3",
  "ExtensionDesc":"This is a description.",
  "OptionSetting":"Options",
  "DetailUrl":"https://www.aliyun.com/",
  "ExtensionCode":"ce4*********086da5",
  "-EventCategoryList":{
   "CategoryCode":"file-change",
   "CategoryName":"File change event"
```

`},`

```json
  "-BindEventList":{
   "EventName":"Pre-event for file committing",
   "EventCode":"commit-file"
```

`},`


`},`


```xml
<ParameterSetting>extension.project.disabled=projectId1,projectId2,projectId3</ParameterS ting>
```

#### GetOptionValueForProject

Queries the option settings of an extension in a workspace.

**Request headers**

This operation does not have operation-specific request headers and uses only common request headers. For more information, see the "Common request parameters" section of the "Common parameters" topic.

**Request parameters**

| Parame ter | Typ e | Positi on | Require d | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RegionId | Strin g | Host | No | default | The region ID. Set the value to default . |
| Extension Code | Strin g | Body | No | ce4*********086da5 | The unique code of the extension. |
| ProjectId | Strin g | Body | No | 234 | The workspace ID. |

**Response parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| Parameter | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| RequestId | String | E6F0DBDD- 5AD**** | The request ID. |
| OptionValue | String | {"cuNumber":"0"} | The returned data. In this example, cuNumber indicates a custom key. |

**Examples**

Sample requests

```
http(s)://[Endpoint]/?Action=GetOptionValueForProject &Common request parameters
```

Sample success responses `JSON` format `{`

```json
 "RequestId":"E6F0DBDD-5AD****",
 "OptionValue":"{\"cuNumber\":\"0\"}"
```

`}` `XML` format

```xml
<RequestId>E6F0DBDD-5AD****</RequestId> <OptionValue>{&quot;cuNumber&quot;:&quot;0&quot;}</OptionValue>
```
